transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I'm completely overwhelmed by constant, intrusive worries about germs and contamination. It has gotten so bad that I spend hours every day washing my hands and cleaning everything around me just to feel safe. I really need help because it's taking over my life.
Do you feel that these thoughts and the need to wash your hands are excessive or unreasonable, even though you feel compelled to act on them?

Yes, absolutely. I know logically that my constant handwashing is completely excessive and doesn't make sense, but the anxiety is just too overwhelming to ignore. It feels like this intense urge takes over, and I have to wash them anyway just to get some relief.

latest_inference.note: The patient's report of intrusive, ego-dystonic thoughts (fears of contamination) and repetitive, time-consuming behaviors (excessive handwashing) performed to alleviate anxiety is highly characteristic of Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder. The patient explicitly acknowledges the irrationality of these behaviors, which supports the diagnosis. No other candidates are currently indicated.
